units.intent: Small micro-framework for writing throughput benchmarks: subclasses mix this in alongside tpunit::TestFixture and call runBench() to time a function over warm-up and measured passes and record its throughput.

objects.name: BenchmarkResult
objects.role: Throughput/elapsed-time/byte-count record for one named benchmark

objects.name: g_benchmarkResults
objects.role: Name-to-BenchmarkResult map shared across the whole benchmark binary; defined in main.cpp

objects.name: BenchmarkBase
objects.role: Mixin base class holding the owning fixture's name

objects.name: BenchmarkBase::setup/teardown
objects.role: Overridable hooks run around each runBench() call

objects.name: BenchmarkBase::runBench
objects.role: Warms up, times N iterations over a vector of inputs, computes MB/s, stores the result, and prints a summary line

objects.name: BenchmarkBase::getInputSize
objects.role: Private helper sizing one input (string or integral only; else a static_assert failure)

name_fit.note: Exactly a base class for benchmarks

naming_quality.note: BenchmarkResult/BenchmarkBase don't carry the repo's `S` prefix used for shared libstuff-style utility types, unlike STable/SData, but that's a minor, acceptable inconsistency for test-only scaffolding

units.intent: Self-contained tpunit fixture benchmarking libstuff's SDeburr::deburr() (accent/diacritic stripping) across ASCII, Latin-1, and mixed-script inputs at normal and high iteration counts.

objects.name: SDeburrBench
objects.role: tpunit::TestFixture + BenchmarkBase; each bench* method times SDeburr::deburr() over a small fixed set of input strings

objects.name: SDeburrBench::benchShortASCII/benchLatin1/benchMixedLong
objects.role: Vary the character set and length of the input

objects.name: SDeburrBench::benchShortASCIIHigh/benchLatin1High/benchMixedLongHigh
objects.role: Same inputs, run at a much higher iteration count to stress steady-state throughput

objects.name: __SDeburrBench
objects.role: Self-registers the fixture with tpunit at static-init time

name_fit.note: Named for exactly the function it benchmarks

units.intent: Self-contained tpunit fixture benchmarking libstuff's SReplaceAll() -- replacing any character from a set with a single replacement character -- across inputs with varying densities and sizes of unsafe-character sets.

objects.name: SReplaceAllBench
objects.role: tpunit::TestFixture + BenchmarkBase; each bench* method times SReplaceAll() over a small fixed set of input strings

objects.name: SReplaceAllBench::benchNoUnsafeChars/benchFewUnsafeChars/benchManyUnsafeChars
objects.role: Vary how many characters in the input need replacing

objects.name: SReplaceAllBench::benchLongUnsafeList/benchURLSafe/benchAlphanumeric
objects.role: Vary the size and shape of the unsafe-character set being matched against

objects.name: __SReplaceAllBench
objects.role: Self-registers the fixture with tpunit at static-init time

name_fit.note: Named for exactly the function it benchmarks

units.intent: Self-contained tpunit fixture benchmarking libstuff's SReplace() across match-count and find/replace length asymmetries.

objects.name: SReplaceBench
objects.role: tpunit::TestFixture + BenchmarkBase; each bench* method times SReplace() over a small fixed set of input strings

objects.name: SReplaceBench::benchNoMatches/benchFewMatches/benchManyMatches
objects.role: Vary how many substring matches are found

objects.name: SReplaceBench::benchLongFind/benchLongReplace
objects.role: Vary whether the find or the replace argument is the long string

objects.name: SReplaceBench::benchShortToLong/benchLongToShort
objects.role: Single-character find vs. a long replacement, and the reverse

objects.name: __SReplaceBench
objects.role: Self-registers the fixture with tpunit at static-init time

name_fit.note: Named for exactly the function it benchmarks

units.intent: Entry point for the standalone benchmark binary: runs the tpunit-registered benchmark fixtures and, given a --baseline ref, also checks out that ref, rebuilds, reruns the benchmarks, restores the working tree, and prints a colored throughput comparison report.

objects.name: runBenchmarks
objects.role: Clears g_benchmarkResults and invokes tpunit::Tests::run() with the given include/exclude filters

objects.name: printComparison
objects.role: Formats a colored baseline-vs-current throughput table (new/improved/regressed/unchanged/removed) to stdout

objects.name: main
objects.role: Parses --baseline/-only/-except/-v/--verbose/--help and orchestrates a plain run or the git-based baseline comparison workflow

objects.name: GREEN/RED/RESET/BOLD
objects.role: File-scope ANSI color codes

objects.name: SIGNIFICANT_CHANGE_THRESHOLD
objects.role: Percent-change cutoff used to classify a result as improved/regressed vs. unchanged

misfits.why: Shells out to git (stash/checkout/rev-parse) and reruns `make bench -j32` from inside the benchmark binary itself; this is build/source-control orchestration that reads more like a CI shell script than a benchmark runner
misfits.suggested_home: a wrapper shell script driving the plain benchmark binary twice

name_fit.note: Conventional entry-point name for the benchmarks binary
